old: A GRS schedule document. `$schema` is where the latest version of this schema lives (the same as this schema's $id), written first so that whoever holds only the document can reach it; a reader never refuses a document over its value. `schedule` is the data; `documentSettings` is how it is drawn when opened; `documentStamp` and `changeLog` record when, by whom and why it changed. Every key is written, null included, so that "the source had no value" and "the value is 0" are never confused. What comes from MS Project XML (MSPDI) keeps its names and codes, so that a round trip loses nothing. Times come in two kinds, for two reasons. Schedule date-times (start, finish, deadline, statusDate, calendar exceptions, comment and highlight boxes) are wall-clock times without a zone, exactly as MS Project writes them, so that they round-trip unchanged; project.scheduleDataTimeZone says whose wall clock they are. They are read as instants to the minute (seconds are cut) and never shifted by an offset. Write each one with its time: a date without a time is read as the start of that day's first working span on a start-side column and the end of its last span on a finish-side column, which is seldom what was meant. A finish-side value is the instant the work ends; a milestone's start and finish are the same instant. A whole-day range (calendar exceptions, boxes) runs from 00:00:00 to 23:59:00. Record instants (documentStamp, changeLog) are UTC, so that every reader sees them in their own local time. A null color or width follows the theme. A custom color gives the light-theme and the dark-theme value ("#light/#dark"; an empty side is drawn with the other), because a readable dark color cannot be derived from a light one.
new: A GRS schedule document. `$schema` is where the latest version of this schema lives (the same as this schema's $id). It is the first property, so that a person who has only the document can find the schema; a reader never refuses a document because of its value. `schedule` is the data; `documentSettings` is how it is drawn when opened; `documentStamp` and `changeLogEntries` record when, by whom and why it changed. A property with no value is omitted: null is never written, and an empty array [] is never written. So "the source had no value" (the property is absent) and "the value is 0" are never confused. What comes from MS Project XML (MSPDI) keeps its names and codes, so that nothing is lost when the file goes to MS Project and back. Times come in two kinds, for two reasons. Schedule date-times (start, finish, deadline, statusDate, calendar exceptions, comment boxes) are wall-clock times without a zone, exactly as MS Project writes them, so that they come back unchanged; project.scheduleDataTimeZone says whose wall clock they are. They are read as instants to the minute (seconds are cut) and never shifted by an offset. Write each one with its time: a date without a time is read as the start of that day's first working span on a start-side property and the end of its last span on a finish-side property, which is seldom what was meant. A finish-side value is the instant the work ends; a milestone's start and finish are the same instant. A calendar exception runs from 00:00:00 to 23:59:00. A range of whole days (a highlight box, the fit span) is written as firstDay and lastDay (YYYY-MM-DD), both included. Record times (schemaVersion, buildVersion, documentStamp, changeLogEntries) are UTC (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ), so that every reader sees them in their own local time. A color is one of three kinds: {"kind":"theme"} follows the theme, {"kind":"palette","name":...} is a named color of the palette, and {"kind":"custom","light":...,"dark":...} gives a value for each theme. In a custom color, each side is {"value":"#rrggbb","source":...}: "chosen" when a person picked it, "derived" when GRS made it from the other side. You may omit one side; GRS derives it when it opens the file. Where a color property may be omitted, an absent color means that part is not drawn.

new: Absent keys. A key that always holds a value is required. A key with no value is omitted: never write null, an empty string, an empty list or an empty object. A color is {"kind":"theme"}, {"kind":"palette","name":…} or {"kind":"custom","light":{"value":"#rrggbb","source":"chosen"},"dark":…}; an absent color key draws nothing. A custom color may omit one side: GRS derives it on load (HSL lightness 1 - L) and writes it with source "derived". Box fills always hold a color; hide one with fillTransparencyPercent 100. ⏎ Sizes. A key ending in Px is a length in CSS pixels at displayScalePercent 100; the drawing multiplies it by displayScalePercent / 100 and never by the zoom. Percent is a percentage (100 is the whole or the same size). Ratio multiplies a default (1 is the default). Fraction is a position inside one thing, from 0 up to but not including 1. dayWidthPx is the width of one day; verticalZoomRatio and taskGroupAutoExpandDepth are the vertical zoom. ⏎ Names. A task and a task group need no name; an unnamed one omits name.
